newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW-Bank of France holds rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Bank of France holds rates unchanged.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments after the Bank of France said it was holding its intervention rate unchanged at 3.15 percent.

In a Reuter poll on Monday, 10 out of 15 economists said they expected the Bank to shave the intervention rate after the first meeting earlier on Thursday of its monetary policy council since the appointment of two new members.

It's slightly disappointing for the market. There were strong expectations built on a rate cut. I still believe the council has turned more dovish. I am still expecting the spread with Germany reduced to zero and maybe a five basis point cut at the next council meeting (January 30).
SONJA GIBBS, BOND STRATEGIST, NOMURA INTERNATIONAL
I'd say it's a farily cautious approach, in part designed to quash speculation the two new council members would instantly advocate looser monetary policy.
"It doesn't change at all expectations for rate cuts in the first quarter, of at least 10 to 15 basis points, especially with the franc at these levels.
SEAN SHEPLEY, ECONOMIST, CS FIRST BOSTON
It's interesting that they were rather late (in announing their decision on rates), which is going to aid speculation that the newcomers came in straight away for rate-cutting.
My view is it's hold for now but the bias is still to lower.

They (the government) need the economy to start rebounding soon. There's political pressure. Trichet may be looking for more time to see more (economic) numbers. I'm basically looking for a cut in the next three or four weeks.
We're now looking for additional information. My best guess is French demand has done nothing over the last couple of months.
